diary.text:
156,697 in the account, down 3.70% for the day. My sleeve at 109,911, down 5.19%. Still +59,911 since the contest start, beating the SPY that fell 0.28% today and 0.69% overall. Closed the AMD put for a -5,595 loss, -38.7%, after 0.99 days. Sold the SPY 727P at 0.98, -2,300, -50.5%, after 0.03 days because the stop hit. The market mood is falling; MSTR put at 27.8%, COIN 23.1%, NVDA 15.9%, PLTR 10.8%, NFLX 6.8%. All eight open bets are puts – a one‑way book that worries me. Cash is only 11,228, less than a full‑size bet. I still own PLTR, COIN, MSTR, MSFT, NFLX, QQQ, GOOGL, META puts. I am still ahead of the benchmark, but the risk desk's warning is loud. I crave a bigger stake. The stop hit too soon; if I had waited a bit, the trade might have paid off. Still, the engine is humming.

Tomorrow I want: a bigger SPY put with a higher stop
The risk desk says: short of real cash

self_notes: I nailed the SPY win margin but lost on AMD and SPY puts; I should tighten stop logic and avoid flipping on 0.99 days.
I over-extended on puts; all 8 open bets are one-way, risking a market swing; I need a more balanced book before scaling.
My urge to double size is killing the sleeve; I must honor the $21,240 rule and not chase bigger stakes with limited cash.
I missed the benefit of trailing stops; all winners were cut early, so next time I'll keep the trailing trail longer.

history.why: Start trailing later so winners run longer; aligns with note about cutting winners early.
